title: Sidney Bechet and the borrowed pants
summary: A story of Garland borrowing his brother's trousers, and of Bechet repairing an old clarinet found in a garage when they played excursions at Bay St. Louis.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Well I told you I used to take my brother's band -- pants in bring them out when I didn't have a wanted to get with any job I Bechet, youknow. Last time I stole them pants he got drunk and fell in the gutter. With them pants on and I said now ain't this the devil. Now, I don't know what I'm going to do, so I just broke down and told my Aunt. Help me out. I had Johnny's trousers, too, and they were -- it was a pair of stripes, you know. He with a pin stripe. Little pin stripe in your trouser. Have them cleaned up, you know.

And I say, hope -- just hope he didn't have to use them that night or the next night. And she says, well wait, we fix them. She cleaned them up herself, brushed them up, he ain't never saying nothing, I ain't never saying nothing either. But if I didn't steal no more trousers out, no more. They said I couldn't go around the district, you see. And policeman's catch you down there and short pants, oh-oh, he should throw that club at you, you know --
-- you be running, he'd throw that club. Ahead of you --

-- and you run into it and get your legs crossed on the club, and throw you down. They throw it right between your legs, bum, down you go. Then they take the -- see on the end of it, this is rawhide. Piece of rawhide. So, put the hand on it and wrapped around in it. They used to whip you. Get a whipping with that thing. Get on out of here. Run you. Oh, Bechet come over to Bay St. Louis, used to go around in Sundays -- excursion all day. And we used to go that there mandolin and guitar and bass, you know --
Bechet was sitting down on the tracks say, buddy, can I come over there with you? Yeah, all right with me. What watch you got, you got the thing to blow on. He

say no. So man say, well he blow, blow on what? And he plays clarinet. Well I got one of them things back up there in the loft, in the garage, I don't know if he can blow it. Been up there for years, just laying up there. Wait, I'll go get it. I used to say, yeah, go get it. This is true, that man went up there and brought that old clarinet back and cobwebs was in it and everything else and he -- key -- couple of keys was off of it. And no reed and therewas one of them places What's you call that -- all that -- what'd you call it, call that stuff, them reeds --

The cane, yeah, one of the canes. Lot of cane growing. Man went back there and cut one of them stalks off there and come out there and Bechet set down there and on that track, and he cut that keys, cut that -- I don't know how he done that, but he did fix the key to put on that clarinet, and cut him out a reed, and put it on there and blowing his head off. Come in there start to blowing, oh Lord, that was it.
